name: No impairment indicator process -> unrecognised impairment risk
rationale: Impairment is only recognised if indicators are first noticed; without a process to look for them, carrying amounts can remain overstated. The rule directs the auditor to evaluate management's assessment (or its absence), to independently identify indicators through analytical procedures, and to test measurement where indicators exist.
